This page describes how traffic enters the legacy Docker Compose stack (pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration): the nginx front door, the per-product subdomain scheme, and the host port map. The Kubernetes platform replaces all of this with Traefik — see Ingress & network edge for the counterpart.

The nginx front door

The stack runs two nginx containers built from the same image (pvarki/nginx:1.31-d<release>, built from the repo's nginx/ directory). A one-shot nginx_templates container delivers the config templates into a shared volume; each nginx instance copies the directory named by NGINX_TEMPLATE_DIR and renders it with its environment variables through the stock nginx envsubst entrypoint. Both instances terminate TLS with the same Let's Encrypt certificate that miniwerk fetched into the le_certs volume (/le_certs/rasenmaeher/fullchain.pem + privkey.pem), with TLS 1.2/1.3 and a shared cipher policy from includes/le_common_settings.conf.

**rmnginx** (template dir templates_rasenmaeher) publishes host port NGINX_HTTPS_PORT (default 443) and defines three server blocks:

  • **<domain>** — the open front page. Serves the Deploy App UI as static files from the rmui_files volume, proxies /api/ to rmapi:8000, serves the CA chain from the ca_public volume at /ca/public/, proxies /ca/crl/ to rmapi's CRL endpoint and /ca/ocsp to the CFSSL OCSP responder (ocsp:8889). No client certificates are involved — this is where users enroll before they have one. The config also 301-redirects HTTP to HTTPS.
  • **mtls.<domain>** — same UI and API, but with client-certificate verification: ssl_client_certificate /ca_public/ca_chain.pem with ssl_verify_client optional, plus live OCSP verification on every handshake — see PKI: CFSSL & miniwerk (legacy). Requests without a valid certificate are 302-redirected to https://<domain>/error?code=mtls_fail. Verified requests are forwarded with identity headers: X-ClientCert-DN, X-ClientCert-Serial, X-SSL-Client-Verify, X-SSL-Client-Fingerprint. A /ui/ location serves product UI bundles from the shared ui_files volume. Note the ssl_crl directive is present but commented out — OCSP is the active revocation path.
  • **synapse.<domain>** — plain TLS proxy to synapse:8008 (the Matrix client-server API handles its own authentication; uploads allowed up to 100M).

**productsnginx** (template dir templates_consolidated) is the second front door, for product integration APIs, publishing two host ports:

  • :4626 (NGINX_HTTPS_PRODUCT_PORT) — client certificate required (ssl_verify_client on; anything unverified gets a 401), same live OCSP check. A map $host block fans requests out by subdomain: tak.<domain> (and mtls.tak.<domain>) → takconfig:8003, bl.<domain> → blapi:3000, mtx.<domain> → rmmtx:8005, matrix.<domain> → matrixrmapi:8012, fake.<domain> → rmfpapi:8001 (dev). The TAK upstream is addressed as takconfig because all TAK containers share that container's network namespace (network_mode: "service:takconfig") — the actual listener is takrmapi.
  • :4627 (NGINX_HTTPS_EPHEMERAL_PRODUCT_PORT) — no client certificate (ssl_verify_client off), routing only /ephemeral/api to the TAK integration. This exists for the ATAK autoimport flow, where the device downloads its enrollment package before it has a certificate.

Both instances resolve upstream names through Docker's embedded DNS (DNS_RESOLVER_IP, default 127.0.0.11) and expose an internal healthcheck listener on :5666. This diagram maps the full edge:

The subdomain model

Every product lives under its own subdomain of a single SERVER_DOMAIN, and the whole namespace is derived from one environment variable on the miniwerk service: MW_PRODUCTS ("tak,kc,bl,mtx,matrix,synapse" in the production composition). miniwerk — "minimal KRAFTWERK emulation" — is a one-shot container that runs miniwerk init at stack start and exits; postgres, openldap, rmapi and rmnginx (among others) gate on service_completed_successfully for it, so effectively the whole stack waits.

For each listed product plus kc (Keycloak), miniwerk expands the FQDN list as <product>.<domain> and mtls.<product>.<domain>, adds mtls.<domain> (the MW_SUBDOMAINS default is mtls) and the bare <domain>. It then:

  1. Writes the kraftwerk manifest JSON for each product into /pvarkishares/<product> (the kraftwerk_shared_* volumes) — this is how products learn their own FQDNs and the rmapi endpoints.
  2. Fetches one Let's Encrypt certificate covering all of those FQDNs as SANs — the certbot mechanics live in PKI: CFSSL & miniwerk (legacy).
  3. Copies the result to the le_certs volume, from which both nginxes and the TLS-terminating services read the same certificate — the full consumer list is on PKI: CFSSL & miniwerk (legacy).

blocks.html:
The consequence of this design: DNS is your job. Every FQDN in that list must be a real A record pointing at the server's WAN address before the stack starts, or the HTTP-01 challenge fails. The README lists the full set (domain, kc.domain, tak.domain, bl.domain, mtx.domain, matrix.domain, synapse.domain, and their mtls.-prefixed twins). Renewal caveats live on PKI: CFSSL & miniwerk (legacy).

For convenience, rmnginx also carries a redirect map: hitting a product subdomain on the main HTTPS port bounces you to that product's real user-facing port — tak.<domain> → :8443, mtx.<domain> → :9888, kc.<domain> → :9443/admin/RASENMAEHER/console/, bl./matrix. → :4626.

Local development uses the same model without owning a domain: docker-compose-local.yml defaults SERVER_DOMAIN to localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi, whose public DNS records (including the mtls. and product subdomains) resolve to 127.0.0.1 — real hostnames that point at your own machine, no /etc/hosts edits. The local composition moves HTTPS to :4439 (https://localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:4439), sets MW_MKCERT=true (mkcert instead of Let's Encrypt), and adds the fake test product to MW_PRODUCTS.

Port map

Host ports published by the production composition (docker-compose.yml):

Host port Published by Carries
80 miniwerk ACME HTTP-01 challenge during cert issuance (container exits afterwards; nothing serves host port 80 at runtime)
443 (NGINX_HTTPS_PORT) rmnginx Deploy App UI + rmapi /api, CA material /ca/public, CRL, OCSP; mtls.* and synapse.* server blocks
4626 (NGINX_HTTPS_PRODUCT_PORT) productsnginx Product integration APIs, client certificate required
4627 (NGINX_HTTPS_EPHEMERAL_PRODUCT_PORT) productsnginx TAK ephemeral autoimport downloads, no client certificate
9443 keycloak Keycloak's own TLS (KC_HTTPS_PORT: 9443, --https-client-auth=request) — kc.<domain> traffic bypasses nginx entirely
1636 openldap LDAPS
8089 takconfig TAK client connections (TLS streaming CoT)
8090–8094 takconfig Reserved for TAK data feeds
8443 takconfig TAK admin/web UI
9000–9002 takconfig TAK federation
1936 mediamtx RTMPS
8322 mediamtx RTSPS
8890 (tcp+udp) mediamtx SRT
9888 mediamtx HLS
9889 mediamtx WebRTC
9996 mediamtx Playback of recorded streams
9997 mediamtx MediaMTX control API

Notes: all TAK service containers (takmsg, takapi, takreten, takplug, takrmapi) share takconfig's network namespace, so its published ports serve them all. TAK's raw ports and MediaMTX's streaming ports do their own TLS with the same miniwerk-fetched certificate — they never pass through nginx. The README's "needed ports" list also mentions 8446, 9446 and 4666; those do not appear in the current compose file (stale entries — the live values are 8443, 9443 and 4626).

Contrast with the Kubernetes platform

The Kubernetes platform collapses this edge into a single Traefik deployment — details live in Ingress & network edge and Edge mTLS & callsign checks, but the mapping is:

Legacy (compose) Kubernetes
rmnginx + productsnginx containers One Traefik instance in traefik-system
envsubst-rendered nginx server blocks IngressRoute resources per host
ssl_verify_client optional / on TLSOption mtls-optional / mtls-strict
Product APIs on dedicated host ports :4626/:4627 Per-product hostnames (tak., mtx., matrix.<domain>) on plain 443
X-ClientCert-DN / X-ClientCert-Serial headers set by nginx Reproduced by the legacy-mtls-headers Traefik plugin for backends that still expect them
Raw TCP/UDP host ports (TAK, MediaMTX) NodePort (local kind) / LoadBalancer (cloud) Services bypassing Traefik

For the certificate and revocation side of this contrast (miniwerk vs cert-manager, OCSP vs callsign-validity), see PKI: CFSSL & miniwerk (legacy). Keycloak is the constant — in both stacks it terminates its own TLS on 9443 and requests (but does not require) client certificates itself.
